kit.name: ELEGOO UNO R3 Super Starter Kit

identity.manufacturer: generic, widely cloned part number; the datasheet fetched is from XLITX Technology, but the same 5161AS numbering and pinout is used by many Chinese LED display makers
generic_equivalents: other 0.56 inch common-cathode single-digit displays with the same 10-pin layout
identity.package: 10-pin through-hole DIP-style 7-segment display, 0.56 inch (14.2 mm) digit height

function.one_sentence_plain_english: Eight little LEDs arranged to draw any digit 0-9 (plus a decimal point), all sharing one ground pin.
function.what_it_is_used_for: Used to show a single number, like a counter, a temperature reading, or one digit of a clock.
function.how_it_works_briefly: Seven LED bars (segments a-g) plus one dot (dp) are arranged in the classic figure-8 pattern. This is the common-cathode version, so all 8 LEDs share one ground (cathode) connection. The Arduino lights up whichever segments it needs by sending +5V, through a current-limiting resistor, to each segment pin. Turning on segments a, b, c, d, e, f (but not g) draws a '0', for example.

pins.pin_1_identification: Confirmed from the datasheet's dimension diagram: hold the display face-up with the decimal point dot in the bottom-right corner (normal reading orientation). Pin 1 is the leftmost pin on the front (bottom) row of legs.

electrical.operating_voltage: driven at 5V through a series resistor per segment; not powered directly
electrical.typical_current: 10 mA per segment (the datasheet's forward-voltage test condition)
electrical.max_current: 30 mA continuous per segment; 200 mA peak per segment at 1/10 duty cycle, 10 kHz (datasheet absolute maximum ratings)
electrical.logic_level: 5V logic; each segment needs a current-limiting resistor (commonly 220-330 ohm) between the Arduino pin and the segment, it is not directly logic-level driven

visual_identification.shape_and_size: Black rectangular plastic housing about 14 mm tall (digit height) and roughly 19 mm overall including pins, about 12.6 mm wide, with a figure-8 shaped red display window on the front and a small round dot (decimal point) at the bottom-right corner. Ten thin metal legs come out the bottom, 5 per row, front and back.
visual_identification.color_and_markings: Black plastic body, red digit segments visible through the front window (grey/dark red when off). Usually no printed part number on the part itself.
visual_identification.printed_text_to_look_for: Usually none on the display itself; if there is a print or sticker, look for '5161' as the model family.
easily_confused_with: the 4-digit 7-segment display in this kit (also black with red segments, but shows four figure-8 windows instead of one)
a small LED bar-graph or matrix display

example_connections.uno_pin: digital pin, e.g. D7, through a 220-330 ohm resistor
digital pin, e.g. D6, through a 220-330 ohm resistor

required_extra_parts: one 220-330 ohm resistor per segment pin used (up to 8 for all segments plus dp)
wiring_to_uno.arduino_library: none required for basic use (direct digitalWrite per segment); the SevSeg library simplifies driving it if desired

handling_notes: always use a series resistor; connecting a segment straight to 5V with no resistor can burn out that LED segment
legs are thin and can bend
common_mistakes: wiring it as if it were common anode (sending GND to segments and 5V to the common pin) when it is actually common cathode, so nothing lights up
leaving both common pins (3 and 8) unconnected, so the whole display stays dark even though only one needs to be wired since they are joined internally

symptoms_and_causes.likely_cause: common pin not connected to GND, or common/anode logic reversed
symptoms_and_causes.check: confirm pin 3 or 8 goes to GND and that the circuit treats this as common cathode, not common anode

symptoms_and_causes.symptom: wrong segments light up or the digit looks scrambled
symptoms_and_causes.likely_cause: segment pins wired to the wrong Arduino pins in code
symptoms_and_causes.check: re-check each segment pin against the datasheet map: A=7, B=6, C=4, D=2, E=1, F=9, G=10, DP=5

symptoms_and_causes.symptom: a segment is dim or appears burned out
symptoms_and_causes.likely_cause: missing or undersized series resistor, exceeding the 30 mA continuous rating
symptoms_and_causes.check: measure the in-circuit resistor value; should be 220-330 ohm for a 5V supply

troubleshooting.how_to_test_with_a_multimeter: Set a multimeter to its diode-test function. Touch the negative probe to pin 3 or 8 (common) and the positive probe to any segment pin; that segment should light up dimly, confirming both the segment map and that this part is common cathode.

confidence.notes: Every US retailer fetch attempted (Amazon x3, Jameco) failed with HTTP 403 or 500, likely bot blocking, so the single-unit retail price is taken from a Philippine electronics shop and converted to USD at an approximate September 2026 rate (~56 PHP/USD). The manufacturer's own bulk factory price ($0.45 per 100-piece minimum order from XLITX) is far lower per unit than any real single-piece retail price and was not used as the headline number for that reason, though the datasheet from that same source was used for all pin and electrical specs.
